Ranch Park: streets and boundaries

items.t: The pocket takes its name from Ranch Park itself, a City park the City describes as a local playground and open grass area for residents.
Ranch Park Elementary, 2701 Spuraway Avenue, sits inside the pocket and is the street-level anchor most residents use to place the neighbourhood.

blocks.text: Ranch Park: the housing stock

items.t: The slope is the defining physical fact of the stock: British Columbia Hydro (BC Hydro) states the elevation change between the top of the slope at Spuraway Avenue and Pinnacle Street and the Como Lake Substation at Como Lake Avenue and Lougheed Highway is 170 metres, so lots step down the hillside rather than sitting flat.

blocks.text: Ranch Park: rules that affect buyers

items.t: A creek, a steep slope or a pre-1945 house on or next to the lot means the City wants the owner to contact Development Services before designing a small-scale project — the steep-slope trigger is the live one on Spuraway Avenue lots.

A BC Hydro underground transmission corridor runs through the neighbourhood between Lougheed Highway and Spuraway Avenue, so a buyer planning additions or excavation should confirm the corridor and any registered easement against the lot's title before designing.

blocks.text: Ranch Park: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Ranch Park's own park is small and local in scale: the City lists a playground, outdoor fitness equipment and alcohol-permitted status, not sports fields or courts.

Childcare has operated at the elementary school for decades: Ranch Park Kids Place, at 2701 Spuraway Avenue, states it has provided care for children ages 2.5 to 12 since 1985, with before- and after-school and summer programs.

The BC Hydro corridor work will be visible before construction starts: pre-work pruning and vegetation removal along the corridor was expected to resume in August 2026, ahead of the spring 2027 construction start.
The City lists the BC Hydro partial cable replacement among its external partner projects and confirms the same 1.3-kilometre scope, so corridor notices may come from either BC Hydro or the City.

blocks.text: Ranch Park: development and new projects

items.t: BC Hydro Partial Cable Replacement Project, utility corridor between Spuraway Avenue and Pinnacle Street and the Como Lake Substation at Como Lake Avenue and Lougheed Highway, BC Hydro, underground transmission cable: 1.3 kilometres of 1970s oil-insulated cable replaced with an oil-free line, with duct banks at road intersections — status: vegetation clearing summer 2026 to winter 2027, construction spring 2027 to about 2029, in service winter 2028 (as of November 3, 2026).

blocks.text: Ranch Park: costs and taxes

items.t: One city-wide item applies the same here as elsewhere in Coquitlam: the City is a designated taxable area for the provincial Speculation and Vacancy Tax, so a residential owner in Ranch Park must complete the annual declaration.

blocks.text: Ranch Park: getting around

items.t: Route 153 is the pocket's bus: it runs from Braid Station via Como Lake Avenue and Mariner Way — with stops on Mariner Way at Hawser Avenue and Daybreak Avenue, on the pocket's west edge — to Coquitlam Central Station.

Both ends of route 153 are SkyTrain stations: Braid Station on the Millennium Line and Coquitlam Central Station on the Millennium Line Evergreen Extension, which is also the West Coast Express terminus.
Driving access runs downhill: Mariner Way connects the pocket to Barnet Highway, and Como Lake Avenue connects it to Lougheed Highway at the bottom of the slope.

blocks.text: Ranch Park: risks and due diligence

items.t: Slope is the first check on any Spuraway Avenue lot: the City flags lots with a steep slope on or next to them for early Development Services contact before small-scale building, and the pocket's grade is documented by BC Hydro at a 170-metre elevation change.

Check the title for the BC Hydro transmission corridor and any easement before planning excavation, pools or additions, because the corridor crosses the neighbourhood between Lougheed Highway and Spuraway Avenue and will be an active construction zone from 2027.

River flood risk is checked, not assumed: the City's floodplain mapping covers the Coquitlam, Fraser and Pitt rivers, and the mapping report does not assign a flood level to individual hillside lots in this pocket.

blocks.text: Ranch Park home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

32 houses sold in Ranch Park with a median price of $1,485,000 (the middle half sold between $1,384,625 and $1,796,000), taking a median of 24 days to sell at 95.6% of the last list price; 9% sold above list. They had a median $579 per square foot, a median year built of 1973 and a median lot of 8,911 square feet. 6 townhomes sold in Ranch Park with a median price of $622,500, taking a median of 11 days to sell at 95.5% of the last list price; 0% sold above list. They had a median $422 per square foot, a median year built of 1977 and a median strata fee of $307 a month.

faq.q: How many homes are for sale in Ranch Park?
faq.a: At the end of October 2026 the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® figures showed 17 houses and 2 condos and townhomes listed in Ranch Park. Those are month-end counts and they move daily, so ask Jared for a current list.

faq.q: Is Ranch Park a buyers’ or sellers’ market?
faq.a: In October 2026, houses had a sales ratio of 24% (a sellers’ market); condos and townhomes had 50% on only 2 listed, too few to read as a market type. The sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed; on the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers. One month in one community is a small sample, so look at the monthly table above before you decide.

faq.q: How many homes sold in Ranch Park from June to October 2026?
faq.a: 13 houses and 4 condos and townhomes sold in Ranch Park over those 5 months; detached houses peaked in September with 4 sold and condos and townhomes peaked in June with 2 sold.

faq.q: How big is Ranch Park compared with the rest of Coquitlam?
faq.a: In October 2026, Ranch Park held 4.5% of the 378 detached houses listed in Coquitlam and 0.3% of the 779 condos and townhomes listed in Coquitlam.

faq.q: What mix of houses and condos is for sale in Ranch Park?
faq.a: In October 2026, houses made up 89.5% of the 19 homes listed in Ranch Park and condos and townhomes made up 10.5%; of the 5 that sold, houses were 80.0% and condos and townhomes 20.0%.

faq.q: Are there more or fewer homes for sale in Ranch Park than in June?
faq.a: Listings of detached houses fell from 41 in June to 17 in October 2026 (−58.5%); condos and townhomes was 1 in June and 2 in October 2026, too few (under 3) to call a rise or fall.

faq.q: Which schools are in or beside Ranch Park?
faq.a: Ranch Park Elementary, at 2701 Spuraway Avenue, is inside the pocket and serves kindergarten to Grade 5. The middle and secondary schools for this part of southwest Coquitlam are Hillcrest Middle School, 2161 Regan Avenue, for Grades 6 to 8, and École Dr. Charles Best Secondary, 2525 Como Lake Avenue, for Grades 9 to 12. School District No. 43 (Coquitlam) assigns by home address, so confirm any specific house in the district locator.

faq.q: What is the BC Hydro work planned in the neighbourhood?
faq.a: BC Hydro is replacing a 1.3-kilometre section of 1970s underground, oil-insulated power cable with a new oil-free line along the existing utility corridor between Lougheed Highway and Spuraway Avenue. Vegetation clearing runs from summer 2026 into winter 2027, construction is expected to begin in spring 2027 and take about two years, and the new line is scheduled in service in winter 2028.

faq.q: Does the slope affect an older house here?
faq.a: Yes, in two practical ways a buyer can verify. BC Hydro states past leaks occurred at the existing cable's joints because of pressure from the 170-metre elevation change, which is a reminder of how much grade the pocket carries. The City also flags any lot with a steep slope on or next to it for an early talk with Development Services before a small-scale multi-unit design.

faq.q: Is Ranch Park in a river floodplain?
faq.a: The City's mapped river floodplains are the Coquitlam, Fraser and Pitt river floodplains, and this pocket sits on the slope above them rather than behind a dike. The local water question is slope drainage and the creek corridors below the pocket, not river flooding. A specific lot still needs checking on City mapping, because the floodplain study is a river study and does not grade individual hillside lots.

faq.q: What did houses in Ranch Park sell for?
faq.a: 32 houses sold in Ranch Park between November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026, with a median price of $1,485,000.

faq.q: How long do houses take to sell in Ranch Park?
faq.a: The median was 24 days from listing to sale, and homes sold at a median 95.6% of the last list price (9% sold above list), for sales November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.
